note: What a table client is given, and the whole of it (SEC-14, SEC-15). It is BUILT from a sealed version, a mask and an audience — never derived by deleting keys from a GM payload — so the schema forbids everything outside the type's revealable ALLOWLIST (1kg.5.3's per-field `revealable` rule), and the invalid examples below are the canary suite in shape form. content_kind is a discriminator whose only v1 member is `document` (ADR 7.4): adding a member later IS a version bump, and what the reservation buys is that a v1 table client shows its neutral placeholder instead of failing to parse. A field carries its KEY and its VALUE and nothing else: the heading is the registry's label for (type, key), which the table bundle already holds, so there is no free-text member on the wire for a title, an alias, a filename or an id to ride in (TABLE-3). The page title is still built from the projection, so the document's name appears only if `name` is masked. An asset is a per-slot TableAssetRef handle, never the GM-side asset_id (SEC-15, REVEAL-21). The examples marked `applies_to: ["server"]` are refused by the server and STRIPPED by the client, and both halves are pinned: the emitter is the confidentiality boundary, because by the time a table client parses, the bytes are on the device. 1kg.7.2 therefore validates every frame it emits against the Pydantic model, and T-1's canaries assert on the RAW response bytes, never on a parsed result.

valid.name: a name and a portrait on the table
one prose section and nothing else

fields.value: She walks into the water and is gone.

valid.name: the common fields alone, on a type that declares more
the stat cells a party may read

value.name: Chill Touch
value.text: Melee spell attack, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 10 necrotic damage.

valid.name: an ability block with a score the creature lacks left out
a list of rumours, the text_list branch

value: The bell still rings under the water.
No one born in the village will swim.

valid.name: a count that is legitimately zero
a client strips a field a newer server added

invalid.name: the GM-side asset reference
invalid.why: SEC-15, REVEAL-21: a table client gets a per-slot handle that dies with its slot, never the asset_id — two slots showing one portrait must not be correlatable

invalid.name: the pinned version number
invalid.why: SEC-15: version numbers, authorship, change lists and write revisions never reach a table client — an undeclared key is invalid for the server to emit and stripped by a client, so this is a server example

invalid.name: the reveal epoch
invalid.why: REVEAL-24: the epoch never leaves the GM's channel, or a guest could count narrowings it cannot see — an undeclared key is invalid for the server to emit and stripped by a client, so this is a server example

invalid.name: the audio epoch
invalid.why: SEC-15: neither epoch is a table client's, and audio state travels in its own frame — an undeclared key is invalid for the server to emit and stripped by a client, so this is a server example

invalid.name: another slot's sequence
invalid.why: REVEAL-24, WT-7: per-slot sequences go only to clients entitled to that slot; a sequence here is an inference channel — an undeclared key is invalid for the server to emit and stripped by a client, so this is a server example

invalid.name: the document's title outside the mask
invalid.why: TABLE-3: every label, the page title included, is built from the projection, so a name appears only when `name` is masked — an undeclared key is invalid for the server to emit and stripped by a client, so this is a server example

invalid.name: an asset's filename
invalid.why: AUDIO-29, SEC-15: a filename can be a spoiler, and nothing names an asset to a player — an undeclared key is invalid for the server to emit and stripped by a client, so this is a server example

invalid.name: a key that is never revealable
invalid.why: REVEAL-10, ED-5: tags are gm_only by construction, so a mask can never name them and a projection can never carry them

invalid.name: an identity link in a projection
invalid.why: ED-20, ED-5: `true_identity` is a field npc declares and the registry does not mark revealable, so it is gm_only by construction — the allowlist is the one thing that can say a field may reach a player

fields.value: She is the lich Vashe the Drowned.

invalid.name: an ability block with no scores in it
invalid.why: ED-9: a masked key is present and non-empty in the pinned version, so an ability heading a table is shown always has a cell under it

invalid.name: an ability score the rules cannot produce
invalid.why: a projection carries document values and is bounded exactly as the document is (0 to 99 for an ability score)

invalid.name: an ability key this contract does not define
invalid.why: CANVAS-19: the block is one field with a closed key set, so a seventh score is a shape the builder never produces — an undeclared key is invalid for the server to emit and stripped by a client, so this is a server example

invalid.name: a stat cell cleared to null
invalid.why: ED-9: a document may hold null for a stat the GM has not filled in; a projection of it would draw an empty cell under a masked heading, so the reveal is refused instead

invalid.name: an entry with a heading and no body
invalid.why: REVEAL-5: every masked key is present and non-empty, so a named block reaches a table with its text or not at all

invalid.name: an entry carrying more than a heading and its text
invalid.why: X-10: an entry is plain text on both members; a note, a source or a marker beside them is a channel the builder never opens — an undeclared key is invalid for the server to emit and stripped by a client, so this is a server example

invalid.name: an empty list where a list of rumours belongs
invalid.why: ED-9: a masked key is present and non-empty in the pinned version, so a list that has been cleared is not a live slot

invalid.name: corpus sources beside the text
invalid.why: SEC-15: sources and citation text never reach a table client — an undeclared key is invalid for the server to emit and stripped by a client, so this is a server example

invalid.name: authorship and a changed-field list
invalid.why: SEC-15: who wrote it and what moved are GM-side facts; a player sees text, not history — an undeclared key is invalid for the server to emit and stripped by a client, so this is a server example

invalid.name: the recipient's alias
invalid.why: AUD-11: an alias travels only on the GM's channel, and a table payload never names anyone — an undeclared key is invalid for the server to emit and stripped by a client, so this is a server example

invalid.name: an eligibility class on a field
invalid.why: ED-25, REVEAL-24: a table read checks entitlement, never eligibility, and a classification made for one audience is invisible to every other — an undeclared key is invalid for the server to emit and stripped by a client, so this is a server example

invalid.name: the authorisation revision
invalid.why: ED-25: slot frames are served from slot state and are never gated on a revision, so a table client has no use for one — an undeclared key is invalid for the server to emit and stripped by a client, so this is a server example

invalid.name: a content kind this contract does not define
invalid.why: ADR 7.4: `document` is the only v1 member; a reference excerpt is an amendment and a version bump, which is why a v1 client shows a placeholder rather than parsing it

invalid.name: an empty projection
invalid.why: ED-9: every masked key is present and non-empty in the pinned version, so a live slot always shows something

invalid.name: an empty value
invalid.why: REVEAL-5: the server refuses a mask key that is empty in the named version, so an empty heading can never reach the table

invalid.name: a value that is only whitespace
invalid.why: REVEAL-5, ED-9: a value that trimming empties is a blank heading on a table, and `present and non-empty` has to mean a player sees something — the contract's own trim decides, so both sides agree on what blank is

invalid.name: a list item that is only whitespace
invalid.why: REVEAL-5: the same inside a list — one blank bullet under a masked heading is what `present and non-empty` rules out

value: The bell still rings under the water.

invalid.name: the same key twice
invalid.why: a projection is built from a mask, which names each field once (ED-17)

invalid.name: a value of the wrong kind for its field
invalid.why: the builder emits the type's declared kind; a list where prose belongs means the projection was assembled by hand

invalid.name: a text field over its bound
invalid.why: a projection carries document text and is bounded exactly as the document is (200 for text)

invalid.name: a projection field carrying a label
invalid.why: TABLE-3, SEC-15: a projection carries a key and a value, and the table client renders the registry's label for (type, key) — a heading on the wire would be a free-text channel through which a title, an alias or a filename fits — an undeclared key is invalid for the server to emit and stripped by a client, so this is a server example

fields.label: Sister Ondrey Vashe - v3 - epoch 4 - pt_4c1b9e7a

invalid.name: a masked key a wildcard could have produced
invalid.why: REVEAL-9, ED-8: `all` is refused wherever a field key is named, so a wildcard cannot survive as far as a projection

invalid.name: a revealed name holding a NUL
invalid.why: Requirement 6 (1kg.5.7.2), lead ruling of 2026-09-21: a projection's text refuses exactly what a document's text refuses, so a value a document refuses can never ride in a projection instead. NUL is a C0 control

invalid.name: revealed prose holding an ESC
invalid.why: Requirement 6 (1kg.5.7.2), lead ruling of 2026-09-21: a projection's text refuses exactly what a document's text refuses, so a value a document refuses can never ride in a projection instead. ESC (U+001B) is a C0 control

fields.value: The tunnel is shown in red ink.

invalid.name: a revealed list item holding a right-to-left override
invalid.why: Requirement 6 (1kg.5.7.2), lead ruling of 2026-09-21: a projection's text refuses exactly what a document's text refuses, so a value a document refuses can never ride in a projection instead. U+202E is a bidirectional control

value: The bell still rings under the water.
No one born‮ in the village will swim.

invalid.name: a revealed entry name holding a byte order mark
invalid.why: Requirement 6 (1kg.5.7.2), lead ruling of 2026-09-21: a projection's text refuses exactly what a document's text refuses, so a value a document refuses can never ride in a projection instead. U+FEFF inside a value is an invisible byte order mark

invalid.name: a revealed entry text holding a left-to-right mark
invalid.why: Requirement 6 (1kg.5.7.2), lead ruling of 2026-09-21: a projection's text refuses exactly what a document's text refuses, so a value a document refuses can never ride in a projection instead. U+200E is in the Bidi_Control set, which is refused whole
